subject: Shameless girls
alt: Cartoon: a man in an orange scarf, holding a stick, says: What shameless girls. When we molested them and beat them up, they went and told everyone at the top of their voices. No shame, no values. Beside him a heavy man in glasses, holding a phone, says: Shame, shame, shame, what shameless and ill-bred girls.
chutki: First came the harassment, then the beating, and now the complaint is that the girls screamed and told everyone. The man with the stick feels no shame for what he did. What embarrasses him is that word got out.

The man beside him, phone in hand, clucks his tongue, and his target is the girls too. Dhodapkar's lines catch a society of bystanders that is more uncomfortable with the scream than with the attack. The yardstick of values runs backwards here: whoever stays silent is cultured, and whoever speaks up is shameless.
